blocks.text: In B1-17 you have learned the five most frequent types of ambiguity of voiceless texts (active or passive, verb or name, simple or derived form, verb person, prefix or root) and a five-step strategy. Now that you're reading and translating long articles, you meet the most difficult cases: ⁧الكتاب⁩ which may be the book of the book or the writers of the book; an impersonal passive as ⁧يعلن عن⁩ ; an adjective that, after aiḍāfa, may refer to two names; a pronoun with two possible precedents; a proper name which is also a common word; the Egyptian prints, where they are written ⁧على⁩ It may also be the name ʿAlī. In this unit learn to use clues ( ⁧القرائن⁩ ) in a systematic way, to distinguish the ambiguity that arises from the lack of vowels from what remains also with vowels, and to manage in translation the unresolved cases and the ambiguity desired (G74). Three weeks, in parallel with EGY-18.

Exercise 10 · Example. Do we need vowels? The Arabic child learns to read on vocalized texts; then the vowels disappear little by little, until there is very little left in the newspapers and books. Many people consider it normal: the experienced reader understands the word from context and does not need someone to vocalize it. Reality, however, is more complex. How many times has an experienced reader stopped in front of a word that can be read in two ways? How many times have we heard a conductor misread a news story, why did he only understand the sentence after it was over? I do not ask for everything to be vocalized: it would weigh down the text and slow down reading. However, I propose a solution in the middle: to vocalize the words that can confuse the reader, such as verbs to the passive and their rare names. Technology can help us: there are now automatic vocalization programs that give good results on simple texts. But they are still wrong when a knowledge of the world that the machine does not have is needed to understand: the program does not know that a book cannot chair a Union, nor that the referee who apologized to the public is a man and not a sentence.
